question: The November Q2 GDP estimate measures:
options: Real July–September year-on-year growth at a stated historical base.
Full-year nominal growth.
Identical growth in every sector.
The December annual growth forecast.
explanation: GDP at market prices differs from sectoral GVA; constant-price growth differs from nominal growth. Examine the base, sector contributions and jobs rather than one headline. Caution: This is a quarterly outturn estimate, not full-year growth, a December forecast, or proof every sector grew 8.2%.

question: Withdrawal of selected QCOs means:
options: Product-specific mandatory conformity requirements changed.
All products became exempt from every safety law.
All BIS standards disappeared.
Every change was a permanent economy-wide repeal.
explanation: Mandatory conformity requirements and the underlying existence of a technical standard are distinct. Input-cost relief should be balanced with safety and testing capacity. Caution: Do not say every QCO or every BIS standard was abolished nationwide.

question: Which Labour Code chronology is correct?
options: All central and state rules were finalised years earlier.
November commencement, with detailed rule-making and transition still relevant.
All Codes remained only draft Bills.
Every worker received every benefit on commencement day.
explanation: Enactment, commencement and operational implementation are separate stages; delegated rules fill statutory detail. Connect September drafts and October consultations to this commencement milestone. Caution: Neither “only a draft in November” nor “all detailed rules and benefits fully operational everywhere” is accurate.

question: Under the EPF enrolment window ₹100 represents:
options: Waiver of every past employer obligation.
Specified damages, not the total employer contribution liability.
The value of all interest and administrative charges combined.
A universal monthly benefit to all workers.
explanation: Regularisation differs from cancellation of all liabilities or compulsory new benefits for unrelated workers. Accessible enrolment and credible records can expand coverage. Caution: Do not call ₹100 the total employer liability or extend the relief automatically outside the covered period.

question: Site-specific oil-mine emergency plans differ from:
options: Risk assessment.
Planning for toxic-gas hazards.
A generic checklist proving every hazard is controlled.
Contractor training.
explanation: A generic compliance checklist cannot substitute for a site-specific hazard assessment. Contractor competence and maintenance integrity matter alongside owner duties. Caution: The draft is not proof every site already complied or that every proposed rule had final force.

question: Notification of DPDP Rules means:
options: The parent Act was repealed.
Every rule was deferred identically.
Every processing duty became immediately operative.
Different provisions may have different commencement timelines.
explanation: A notified rulebook can have staggered commencement; institutional establishment and enforceable processing duties differ. Map January consultation to November notification without assuming every draft clause survived. Caution: Do not say every processing duty began on notification day or every provision was deferred equally.

question: Parental verification exceptions for specified institutions imply:
options: A token gives consent for every later purpose.
All education data is exempt from every duty.
Purpose-limited exceptions, not unrestricted commercial reuse.
Healthcare status permits unlimited resale.
explanation: Age assurance and data minimisation must work together; collecting more identity data creates risks of its own. Design accessible alternatives and minimise repeated sensitive-data collection. Caution: Do not treat every education-related data use as exempt or a token as permission for any later purpose.

question: Which Export Promotion Mission pairing is correct?
options: Protsahan—trade finance; Disha—non-financial readiness.
The entire outlay was already disbursed at approval.
Disha—only monetary policy; Protsahan—only heritage.
Both are direct equal cash payments to all citizens.
explanation: Credit constraints, standards compliance and logistics are different bottlenecks requiring complementary interventions. AP marine/MSME exporters need both finance and credible quality/traceability. Caution: An approved envelope is not money already paid; do not reverse the two sub-schemes.

question: The 6,000 MTPA REPM target refers to:
options: Output already produced on Cabinet approval day.
Mineral reserves already mined.
Planned annual integrated magnet capacity.
A monthly cash payment to every manufacturer.
explanation: Reserves, separated oxides, metals, alloys and finished magnets are different supply-chain capabilities. Competitive selection and reliable inputs must accompany capital support. Caution: 6,000 MTPA is planned annual capacity, not output already produced or a measure of mineral reserves.

question: A processed product using a GI ingredient:
options: Always inherits the logo without conditions.
Does not automatically gain GI-logo entitlement under the discussed draft.
Can ignore product standards.
Automatically becomes a new registered GI.
explanation: A GI links origin with a quality or reputation; it is not a generic quality mark for any producer. AP craft/food value chains need authentic producer access and enforcement. Caution: Using a GI ingredient does not automatically entitle a processed product to use the GI logo.

question: Israel FTA terms of reference are:
options: Proof all tariffs were abolished.
The same instrument as every investment agreement.
Evidence the FTA was already in force.
A negotiation milestone distinct from September’s investment treaty.
explanation: Negotiation launch, conclusion, signature and entry into force have different legal consequences. Predictability can benefit trade but depends on final schedules and origin rules. Caution: Terms of reference do not prove tariffs were already eliminated.

question: An export-credit moratorium is:
options: A conditional pause in payments, not automatic debt cancellation.
An unconditional principal write-off.
A universal grant to every exporter.
An abolition of all foreign-exchange reporting.
explanation: A moratorium postpones payments; it does not automatically extinguish principal or interest. Cash-flow relief helps viable exporters survive external shocks. Caution: Do not call the measures an unconditional loan waiver or apply the covered dates to every borrower.

question: The November assent-reference opinion should be read as:
options: Keeping April’s timeline position wholly unchanged.
Endorsing deemed assent as a universal rule.
Rejecting court-prescribed universal timelines while allowing limited directions for prolonged inaction.
Removing every possible response to indefinite inactivity.
explanation: Article 143 advisory jurisdiction differs from ordinary merits adjudication; operative reasoning matters. Link April’s ruling, May’s reference and November’s opinion as a developing constitutional debate. Caution: Do not repeat April’s timeline propositions as an unchanged November position or say every delay is beyond all scrutiny.

question: A direction to establish a Tribunals Commission proves:
options: The new commission was functioning immediately.
A judicial direction, not actual operational establishment.
Every tribunal was abolished.
Executive control over adjudication became unrestricted.
explanation: Appointment design affects independence; a direction to establish a body is not proof the body exists. Executive accountability must not become control over adjudication. Caution: Do not say all tribunals were abolished or the commission was operational immediately.

question: The retrospective-EC review does not imply:
options: The relevance of the 2017 cut-off.
An unrestricted prospective licence for future violations.
A changed position from the earlier May ruling.
A need to preserve legal chronology.
explanation: Exceptional regularisation is not a prospective licence to violate environmental law. Read the review with the earlier May note; retain dated positions instead of silently presenting both as current. Caution: Do not call every future violation regularisable or omit the notification’s cut-off date.

question: The draft Seeds Bill must be distinguished from:
options: Quality regulation.
A traceability framework.
A consultation proposal.
An already enacted replacement and a ban on all traditional seed exchange.
explanation: Seed quality regulation and plant-variety intellectual-property protection are separate regimes. Traceability can deter spurious seeds when inspection, testing and accessible remedies work. Caution: The draft is not an enacted replacement or a ban on every traditional seed exchange.

question: A new PLI application round is not necessarily:
options: Subject to product eligibility.
Linked to verified performance.
A fresh independent budget to add mechanically to every earlier headline.
A policy-stage development.
explanation: New rounds, revised eligibility and realised incremental production are not interchangeable. Specialised grades can matter for defence/power supply chains. Caution: A capacity target is not commissioned production or a guaranteed incentive to every applicant.

question: DRDO–DGA cooperation establishes:
options: Unlimited ownership of all French defence IP.
A completed procurement of every listed platform.
Guaranteed local absorption without skills.
A framework, not automatic delivery of every technology.
explanation: A cooperation instrument differs from delivery of a particular weapon or unrestricted technology ownership. Local absorption needs skilled teams, manufacturing capability and workable IP arrangements. Caution: Do not call an R&D framework a completed procurement or unlimited transfer of all French technology.

question: The revised thermal co-firing policy:
options: Makes every coal plant wholly renewable.
Has differentiated NCR and non-NCR blend requirements.
Mandates the identical NCR blend everywhere.
Eliminates all combustion emissions.
explanation: Torrefaction uses low-oxygen heating; co-firing mixes fuels rather than making coal renewable. Reliable feedstock and pollution safeguards determine practical benefits. Caution: Do not generalise the NCR blend to every plant or assume mixed-fuel combustion is emission-free.

question: The legal-aid anniversary distinguishes:
options: 1987 enactment from 1995 implementation.
Only income-based eligibility with no statutory categories.
1995 enactment from 1987 implementation.
Eligibility only for convicted people.
explanation: Statutory eligibility includes categories as well as prescribed income conditions; income is not the only route. Competent representation and early help matter beyond assigning a lawyer. Caution: 1995 commencement does not mean the Act was enacted in 1995 or aid is only for convicted prisoners.

question: A G20 voluntary minerals framework is:
options: A supranational mining statute.
Political cooperation, not automatically binding domestic law.
A guarantee every announced investment occurred.
A replacement for all national mining permissions.
explanation: G20 political coordination does not create a supranational legislature or automatic domestic law. Assess follow-through and financing, not declarations alone. Caution: Do not treat every target as binding or a political declaration as proof of delivered electrification.

question: COP30’s adaptation-finance signal should not be called:
options: Part of an implementation debate.
A political direction for scaling finance.
Money already paid under an automatically binding commitment.
Relevant to vulnerable communities.
explanation: Mitigation, adaptation and just-transition support address different needs. Distinguish negotiated decisions, presidency initiatives and actual disbursements. Caution: Do not call a presidency roadmap a universally negotiated phase-out or a finance signal a binding paid commitment.

question: One Health links:
options: Human, animal and environmental systems.
Only human hospitals.
A claim every mission stage originated in November.
Only veterinary exports.
explanation: Zoonotic threats cross administrative sectors; data integration requires compatible standards and lawful sharing. AP livestock, aquaculture and public-health systems provide practical convergence settings. Caution: Do not date every approval, institution and launch to the coverage month or equate One Health with only zoonoses.

question: Antimicrobial resistance means:
options: Microorganisms resist treatment, not that a person becomes immune to antibiotics.
The human body becomes immune to every drug.
Appropriate treatment should always be denied.
Only hospitals can contribute to resistance.
explanation: Resistance develops in microorganisms, not because a human body becomes immune to an antibiotic. Prescription audits and diagnostics must coexist with access to necessary treatment. Caution: Do not equate AMR solely with antibiotic use in human hospitals or recommend denial of appropriate therapy.

question: Birsa Munda’s November 2025 commemoration concerns:
options: His 150th birth anniversary.
His birth in an AP tribal community.
The 150th anniversary of every tribal rebellion.
His death in 1875.
explanation: Tribal resistance involved political, economic and cultural claims rather than a single undifferentiated cause. Link historical land alienation to contemporary safeguards without implying all tribal movements were identical. Caution: Do not confuse a birth anniversary with the year of the uprising or relocate him to an AP tribe.

question: A brain–computer interface should not be assumed to provide:
options: Sensitive-data governance challenges.
Potential therapeutic assistance.
Infallible unrestricted access to every private thought.
Task-specific neural-signal interpretation.
explanation: Decoding a limited task signal is not infallible unrestricted reading of every private thought. Consent must address sensitive data, updates and withdrawal possibilities. Caution: Do not call every neural inference accurate or assume ordinary app consent is sufficient for all invasive uses.

question: Farmers’ seed rights under PPV&FR do not imply:
options: A sui generis rights framework.
A balance with breeders’ interests.
Unrestricted branded commercial sale of every protected variety.
An interest in seed conservation.
explanation: Sui generis protection differs from granting patents over every plant; seed-quality law is another layer. Innovation incentives should coexist with conservation and farmer access. Caution: Farmer seed rights do not mean unrestricted commercial branded sales of every protected variety.

question: The CII summit’s MoU totals represent:
options: Reported proposals, not audited realised spending.
Full money already spent.
Verified net jobs already created.
Amounts necessarily additional to every earlier announcement.
explanation: MoU value, financial closure, construction, commissioned assets and net employment are different indicators. Track implementation milestones, cancellations and overlap with earlier announcements. Caution: Headlines saying investment “attracted” do not prove the full amount was already spent or jobs created.

question: A plan for 175 AP MSME parks establishes:
options: A finished viable park in every constituency.
Identical jobs in every constituency.
A geographic ambition, not proof all parks are operational.
No need for market and infrastructure assessment.
explanation: A spatial target is not evidence of serviced land, occupancy or viable enterprises at every site. Evaluate power, logistics, credit, market links and local skills before site-count success claims. Caution: Do not describe all 175 parks as operational or promise identical industries/jobs to every constituency.

question: A parliamentary committee’s work programme is:
options: Proof the government accepted unissued recommendations.
A completed audit conclusion.
An agenda for examination, not a report of findings.
A binding law amending every scheme.
explanation: Agenda-setting, evidence-taking, report adoption and implementation are separate oversight stages. Use the list to identify research gaps rather than cite unissued conclusions. Caution: Do not turn “to examine” into “committee found” or “government implemented”.
